name: Scientific
scope: The civilian scientific enterprise — universities, independent research collaborations, peer-reviewed journals, observatories, scientific instrumentation, professional bodies, civilian funding. International in scope.
excludes: AARO's forensic/analytic work (Military); NASA acting as a federal agency (Government), except its peer-review-style scientific output; Avi Loeb's government advisory role (Government) — only his independent Galileo Project work counts here; scientific testimony at a hearing (the hearing is Legislative).
method: First-principles ladder ordered by scientific commitment, evidential rigor and cost of reversal. Non-ontological: rungs measure the enterprise's acts (studying, publishing, instrumenting, replicating), never the nature of the phenomenon.
read: The spine is the scientific method itself, so the ladder would hold for ball lightning or any once-stigmatized subject. Legitimacy, peer review and a first empirical result are crossed; the frontier is replication, still on preprints. International, unlike the US-only tracks.
summary: Civilian UAP science has crossed the legitimacy, peer-review and empirical-result thresholds, has real instruments and early institutional support, and its most-cited results (VASCO) have now been independently reproduced by three unaffiliated researchers. Its frontier sits inside replication: those replications are still preprints and the field is in active published dispute.
sourcingQuality: Strong — university records + journal DOIs (Nature/Scientific Reports, PASP, MNRAS, Entropy, Sensors). Replication rung rests on named arXiv preprints, flagged.

rungs.title: Formal academic admissibility
rungs.oneLiner: A university formally admits UAP as a research subject. e.g. Würzburg IFEX, 2022.
rungs.firstPrinciples: First move beyond individual curiosity — an established institution accepts UAP within its official research remit. A discrete, irreversible act.
rungs.statusRationale: A university senate made UAP an official research objective. Threshold crossed.

sources.label: Würzburg (JMU) — UAP an official objective of its IFEX centre, 25 Jan 2022

rungs.title: Peer-reviewed scholarly entry
rungs.oneLiner: UAP research enters ordinary peer review. e.g. Knuth et al., Entropy 2019; VASCO.
rungs.firstPrinciples: Publication exposes specific methods/conclusions to disciplinary scrutiny and permanently enters the literature. Binary threshold.
rungs.statusRationale: Peer-reviewed UAP-relevant work exists in ordinary journals. Threshold crossed.

sources.label: Knuth, Powell & Reali, Entropy 21, 939 (2019); + Galileo publication register

rungs.title: Shared methods & evidential standards
rungs.oneLiner: Frameworks exist (Galileo, NASA). Partial: no field-wide adopted standard.
rungs.firstPrinciples: Before studies can be compared, researchers must agree what counts as usable evidence and how to measure it.
rungs.statusRationale: Serious frameworks exist but remain project-specific; no field-wide adopted standard/taxonomy, no authoritative body enforcing adoption.

sources.label: Watters et al., JAI (2023) — multimodal ground-based observatory methods

rungs.title: Peer-reviewed empirical investigation
rungs.oneLiner: A measured empirical result is published. e.g. Villarroel/VASCO (contested).
rungs.firstPrinciples: An actual measured empirical result on a UAP-relevant phenomenon, published and testable. Below dedicated observation because the data can be archival.
rungs.statusRationale: The discrete threshold ('a peer-reviewed empirical UAP-relevant result exists') is met and irreversible. These results are contested — the 22σ figure is an Earth-shadow deficit, not anomalous performance — and Achieved measures that the work occurred, not that its interpretation is settled.

sources.label: Villarroel et al., Nine simultaneous transients, Scientific Reports 11, 12794 (2021)
Villarroel et al., Aligned multiple-transient events in POSS-I, PASP 137 (2025)

rungs.title: Dedicated prospective observation
rungs.oneLiner: Purpose-built instruments (Galileo, UAPx). Partial: coverage/scale can grow.
rungs.firstPrinciples: Purpose-built instruments collect new calibrated data prospectively, vs relying on archives.
rungs.statusRationale: Systems operate, but coverage, triangulation, sensor diversity, calibration, uptime and independent-site replication can all improve substantially.

sources.label: Domine et al., All-Sky Infrared Camera Array, Sensors 25, 783 (2025)

rungs.title: Open & reproducible evidence infrastructure
rungs.oneLiner: Public annotation portal + open datasets. Partial: no complete raw/calibrated archive.
rungs.firstPrinciples: Observations, calibration, metadata, code and provenance accessible enough for outsiders to reproduce or challenge.
rungs.statusRationale: Real open elements function, but no complete prospective UAP dataset with raw files, full calibration, synchronized multimodal timestamps, code and provenance is openly available.

rungs.title: Durable multi-institutional support
rungs.oneLiner: UAlbany endowment, Galileo grant, IFEX. Partial: small, donor-dependent.
rungs.firstPrinciples: Support beyond a single investigator/project/funding cycle.
rungs.statusRationale: More than one institutional base exists, but concentrated, donor-dependent, no NSF-style recurring public programme, no dedicated career pipeline. Sol Foundation (policy think tank) and Nolan's non-mainstream-venue work are watch items, not scored milestones.

sources.label: Richard King Mellon Foundation US$575,000 grant to Galileo Project

rungs.title: Independent testing & replication
rungs.oneLiner: Doherty, Busko, Cann reproduced core VASCO findings. Partial: preprints, active dispute.
rungs.firstPrinciples: Independent teams reanalyse a result, recover observations with independently built methods, or test the phenomenon on separate data/instruments.
rungs.statusRationale: Substantial independent replication has occurred: Doherty reproduced the nuclear-test correlation and Earth-shadow deficit with code written from scratch; Busko found similar transients in independent Hamburg Observatory plates and showed a subclass carries the optical signature of coma (a telescope aberration a plate defect cannot mimic); Cann found detections track the geomagnetic environment. Still Partial: all three are preprints, and the field is in active published dispute (Watters/Knuth critique + Villarroel response). Peer-reviewed convergent replication has not happened.

sources.label: Doherty (arXiv:2604.00056) — reproduced nuclear correlation + shadow deficit
Busko (arXiv:2603.20407) — independent Hamburg plates, coma signature

rungs.title: Convergent replicated knowledge
rungs.oneLiner: No stable UAP finding reproduced across independent methods and teams.
rungs.firstPrinciples: Multiple independent programmes repeatedly obtain a stable, reproducible finding — cumulative knowledge, not one-off results.
rungs.statusRationale: Findings largely share the POSS-I/VASCO data lineage; independent analyses dispute interpretation; no separate observing programme has reproduced the full result peer-reviewedly.

rungs.title: Normal-science integration
rungs.oneLiner: Not routine science; 69% of surveyed faculty fear ridicule (Yingling et al.).
rungs.firstPrinciples: Routine cumulative science — accepted standards, stable funding, training pathways, broad participation, no exceptional stigma.
rungs.statusRationale: Continuing abnormality is documented: a peer-reviewed survey of 1,460 faculty found ~69% reported some concern about ridicule for UAP research.

sources.label: Yingling et al., Academic Freedom and the Unknown, HSSC (2024)

crossTrackNotes: NASA Independent Study Team credited here only for scientific methodology; its agency/administrative facets are Government. Loeb: Galileo Project → here; his government advisory-council role → Government. AARO analysis/materials testing → Military/Government, never here.
